# M3-9: Human-lock detection

- Milestone: M3
- Branch / worktree: `t/M3-9`, `../YNAB_AutoCategorizer.wt/M3-9`
- Depends on: M3-0a, M3-1b
- Touches (exclusive while running): sync/
- Plan refs: §3.1 step 2, R6b, V8
- YNAB access: none
- Deploy: no (smoke: none; ships in M3-17)

## Goal
After each sync, any field a human changed is locked, so finbot never overwrites it.

## Scope
- In the same transaction as the upsert, for the active plan:
  - (a) a transaction with a `done` write_log entry whose current field differs from that entry's after_json → lock that field, source `ynab_edit`.
    Only compare fields present in after_json.
  - (b) a transaction with no `done` write_log entry and no unresolved `intent`, `approved=true` and a real category → lock `category`, source `first_touch`.
- Not locked: unapproved rows carrying a category (YNAB payee memory), and approved rows with no category.
- Skip any transaction with an unresolved `intent` row, so an in-flight write doesn't look like a human edit.
- A backfill pass runs once for a plan with no prior detection, because deltas only carry changed rows.
- Our own write echoing back in a later delta must not lock.
- Counts in the sync summary log; no ids.

## Out of scope
- Closing Slack questions on a lock (M3-10b). Detection for archived plans.

## Acceptance (each must be demonstrably checked)
- [ ] Tests for each rule: (a) divergence, (a) our echo not locking, (b) first touch, unapproved guess not locked, approved with no category not locked.
- [ ] Test: an unresolved intent isn't judged, including the post-crash case where the sync brings back our own PATCH (`approved=true`) before `writer.Reconcile` runs: no lock.
- [ ] Test: the backfill runs once and locks pre-existing approved rows.
- [ ] Test: locks commit or roll back with the rows and cursor.
- [ ] go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./... green

## Result
- Status: DONE
- What changed:
  - `sync/locks.go`: `Syncer.DetectLocks(planID)` turns detection on for the active plan; `detectLocks` runs inside `SyncPlan`'s `Update`, after the upsert and before the cursor save. `Result.Locks` (`LockCounts`: Backfill, Judged, Edit, FirstTouch, SkippedIntent).
  - Rules: (a) each after_json key of the latest `done` write whose current mirror value differs → lock, source `ynab_edit`; `category_id` maps to `store.LockFieldCategory`, other keys keep their YNAB name. Keys the mirror doesn't hold aren't compared; a non-object after_json (delete) names none. (b) no `done` write, `approved=1`, real category → `category` lock, `first_touch`. Any row with an unresolved `intent` is skipped (also when it has an older done write). Deleted rows aren't judged.
  - "Real category": in the mirror's categories and not internal (excludes YNAB's Uncategorized), or named `Inflow: Ready to Assign`. A split parent's sentinel isn't one.
  - `store/lockdetect.go`: `Tx.LockCandidates` (reads through the write tx), `Tx.LockBackfilled`, `Tx.MarkLockBackfilled`. Migration `0009_lock_detection` (plan_id, backfilled_at): the backfill judges every live row once and the mark commits with it.
  - `cmd/app.go`: the syncer runs `DetectLocks(cfg.YNABBudgetID)`; the `sync tick` slog line gains `human_locks` counts. `sync/sync.go` logs the same counts (no ids).
- Acceptance:
  - Rule tests → pass: `go test ./sync -run 'TestDetectLocks|TestDivergent'` (FirstTouch: first touch, unapproved guess, approved w/o category, internal Uncategorized; EchoDoesNotLockButDivergenceDoes; ComparesAgainstTheLatestDoneWrite; UnresolvedIntentIsNotJudged incl. post-crash echo with `approved=true` before Reconcile; BackfillRunsOnce; OtherPlansAreNotJudged; CommitAndRollBackWithRowsAndCursor for both the initial load and a delta).
  - Mutations each fail tests: dropping the intent skip, always-diverge, ignoring `approved`, dropping the backfill mark, dropping the category field map, dropping int→float normalization.
  - `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...` → pass; `go test -race ./sync` → pass.
